questions.question: Why does simply resending the identical prompt after a validation failure tend not to work?
options: The API rate-limits identical requests
A prompt that reliably produces a failing output tends to reproduce the same failure again
Claude caches responses and will always return the same answer
Identical prompts are rejected by the API automatically

questions.question: What should a retry request include to give the model a real chance to self-correct?
options: Just a generic 'validation failed, try again' message
The original document plus the failed attempt and the specific validation error that occurred
A completely different prompt unrelated to the original task
A higher temperature setting to encourage variation

questions.question: What is the hard boundary on what retry-with-error-feedback can fix?
options: It can only fix errors in numeric fields, never text fields
It cannot conjure information that is genuinely absent from the source document
It only works for the first retry attempt, never subsequent ones
It can only be used with schema validation, never semantic validation

questions.question: What's a risk of relying on retries alone when a required field is genuinely missing from the source document?
options: The pipeline runs out of memory
The model may fabricate a plausible-looking value just to satisfy retry pressure and pass validation
The API will return a permanent error and stop working
The document gets permanently corrupted

questions.question: In a well-designed pipeline, which check should run first to handle the 'information genuinely absent from source' case efficiently?
options: A cheap deterministic/keyword presence check on the source, with the retry loop as the fallback for what it can't resolve
An unlimited retry loop with no cap, since eventually it will succeed
A second LLM call to double-check the first model's confidence
Immediately escalate every failure to a human reviewer without any automated check

questions.question: Why can't a naive keyword/literal presence check on the source document be trusted alone to detect missing fields?
options: It's too slow to run at scale
OCR noise, label variants, and non-literal/derived fields can all produce false negatives
It requires a separate paid API call every time
It only works for numeric fields, not text fields
